evidence_items.locator: Opening discussion of Hackett's April 9 speech
evidence_items.explanation: The report records a direct industry admission and describes executives narrowing expectations because of technical complexity. A readable primary transcript was not obtained, so contemporary reporting is used.

evidence_items.locator: Brin's answer about when everyday people could experience self-driving cars
evidence_items.explanation: This establishes the optimistic public forecast invoked in the post, but Brin also qualified his answer and recognized safety challenges. Experiencing the technology is narrower than widespread unrestricted deployment, so this is not treated as an unambiguous failed promise.

evidence_items.locator: Original announcement, paragraph beginning with the October 8 opening
evidence_items.explanation: Waymo had opened a public driverless service before the post. This materially qualifies the surrounding description of only experimental tests, but restricted-area deployment does not refute the narrower claim that development was harder than expected.

evidence_items.locator: Retrospective discussion of the No Hands Across America project
evidence_items.explanation: The university's retrospective documents the 1995 autonomous-steering demonstration and reports that its researchers anticipated gradual development. It supports the historical background while cautioning against treating optimistic expectations as universal.

unresolved_gaps: No representative evidence establishes what a literal majority of people expected.
